config.title: Context Performance

intro.title: Context Performance
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that demonstrates how to optimize performance by using context effectively. You will learn to manage and pass data between components without unnecessary re-renders, using Vue's built-in reactivity system. The main technologies involved are Vue components, reactive state, and props. By the end, you will understand how to structure your app to keep it fast and responsive, even as it grows in complexity.
intro.usecase: In real-world Vue applications, context performance optimization is crucial for complex dashboards with multiple interactive panels like analytics tools or admin interfaces. Developers encounter this when building data tables with filters, nested navigation menus, or multi-step forms where components share state without excessive re-renders. For example, in an e-commerce dashboard showing live inventory, order status, and customer metrics, efficient context management prevents sluggish UI updates when one panel changes. This pattern also appears in collaborative tools like project management apps where team members see real-time updates across different views without performance degradation.

objectives: Construct a Vue application with multiple components that share state via props
Configure a context provider to manage global state efficiently
Apply the useContext hook to access shared state in child components
Manipulate context values to update application state across components
Initialize a performance-optimized context to prevent unnecessary re-renders
Integrate context with local component state for hybrid state management
Control component rendering by selectively consuming context values

steps.hint: Use the ref function you imported earlier to create a reactive reference. The syntax is: const count = ref(0).

steps.title: Define an increment handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your component, create a function named incrementCount that increases the count value by 1 when called.
steps.hint: Define a regular JavaScript function that accesses the count ref's value property and increments it.

<script>
import { ref } from 'vue'

// Define your Vue component here

  setup() {
    const count = ref(0)
    
    // Create your increment handler function here
    
    return {
      count
    }
  }
}
</script>

<template>

</template>

successCriteria: A function named incrementCount is defined that increments count.value by 1.

steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named incrementCount and it increments count.value by 1.

steps.expectedOutcome: The increment handler will now update both reactive values, demonstrating how multiple state updates can affect component re-renders.
successCriteria: The increment handler function updates both count.value and message.value when called.
